notes:
Summary:
- SaaS vendor building KB RAG for customer-facing support and product docs. Focus: embeddings + neural reranker pipeline to improve precision on top results.

Scale & performance profile (customer input):
- Index size: moderate — target 8-12M docs (avg doc ~250-400 tokens).
- Vector dim: ~1536 (current embed model), ~100M total vectors in index (including chunking).
- Traffic: baseline 300 qps; expected bursts up to 1,200 qps during product launches.
- Reranker pattern: ANN retrieves top-50, then LLM reranker on top-10. Reranker invoked ~20-30% of queries (configurable).
- SLA targets: p95 search-only <= 120ms; end-to-end (retrieve + rerank) p95 <= 350ms; p99 <= 700ms (legal redline).
- Cost goals: target cost per user query (end-to-end average) < $0.02; willing to trade small latency increase for 30-40% cost reduction via batching/quantized models.

Technical requirements & preferences:
- Must use hosted_api initially (no private infra at POC). Preference to keep control plane but allow per-customer data partitioning.
- Strong desire for Redis/kv caching of embeddings + prefix caching for repeated queries.
- Routing: route to cheaper model for low-value queries, fallback to higher-quality reranker when confidence threshold low.
- Model preference: quantized transformer variants for rerank (FP16/4-bit), with fast small-model fallback.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, ability to trace a single request through retrieve->rerank.
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML for SRE and admin UI, KMS integration for keys, audit logs retained for 1 year, EU data residency for subset of customer data.

Customer pain / why Redwood:
- Current solution: self-hosted ANN + separate LLM calls for rerank (operational overhead, inconsistent latency under burst).
- Pain points: unpredictable p99 latency, rising cost at scale, complexity of autoscaling reranker containers.
- Quote from CTO: "We need predictable unit economics at 1k+ qps — bursty traffic kills our margins."

POC success criteria (agreed):
- Ingest 10M docs and validate indexing pipeline + memory footprint.
- Meet p95/p99 latency targets under three traffic profiles (baseline, launch-burst, slow-hours).
- End-to-end F1/accuracy comparable to current in-house reranker (+/- 3%).
- Demonstrate per-query cost <= $0.02 with Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, cache hit rate >= 40%).
- Security checklist: SSO, KMS demo, audit log export to customer SIEM.

Open questions / Potential blockers:
- Legal: need explicit 99th-percentile SLA and data residency wording for EU customers.
- Billing: customer requests predictable cost cap option vs pure usage billing.
- Edge case: how Redux (Redwood) handles hot-key queries that eliminate caching benefits.

Sales notes / Next actions (AE/SE):
- 2026-03-15: POC kickoff — ingest 10M docs; SE (Liam) to run perf harness and provide baseline numbers.
- Provide detailed cost model for three traffic profiles (baseline/burst/steady).
- Prepare security deep-dive with PKI/KMS engineer; share audit log export demo.
- Draft SLA language options for legal to review (include p99 remedy and credits).
